subject: Orchid Systems — ops qualification: latency targets, burst plan, and topology
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhang <emily@orchid.systems>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Apr 2029 18:15:00 -0700
Subject: Orchid Systems — ops qualification: latency targets, burst plan, and topology

Emily — thanks again for a productive call today. Quick recap and the items we promised to follow up on. Please skim and correct if I missed anything.

Topline pain / goals we heard:
- Real-time recommendation service (customer personalization) with strict p95 latency target ~<100ms end-to-end for 95% of requests.
- Sustained baseline QPS ~250 req/s with short promotional bursts up to ~400–450 req/s for 2–10 minute windows.
- Mixed model footprint: primary model is a fine-tuned 33B variant for quality; exploring a 7–13B distilled path for cheaper low-fidelity responses.
- EU data residency requirement for production traffic; US for testing.
- Security: SOC 2 in-process; need evidence for private deployment options and KMS integration.

Technical constraints called out on the call:
- Typical prompt length: 80–160 tokens; average response 40–80 tokens.
- HeavyKV reuse: many requests share prefix context for a user session — opportunity for KV/prefix caching.
- Burst pattern origin: orchestrated promotions from their campaign service (spiky, short-lived).

Initial topology notes (from our side):
- We recommend a multi-variant routing plan: primary 33B on Dedicated (EU region) with a cheaper 13B quantized fallback for burst overflow.
- Autoscaling: reserved baseline + short-lived burst pool with warm replicas; target cold-starts <150ms for loading quantized variants.
- Caching: prefix/KV caches at the serving layer to keep p95 latency down during sustained traffic.
- Canary plan: start with limited route (5% traffic) in EU region + synthetic load test before ramp.

Action items we agreed to:
1) Ben/Rachel: share sample QPS/time series and 24h request dump (anonymized). (Attached: orchid_workload_samples.csv)
2) Redwood: run an initial benchmark matrix (33B vs 13B quantized) on EU Dedicated topology and share latency/throughput curves.
3) Security: Emily to share the current questionnaire and any must-have controls (SOC evidence).
4) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra team — proposed window: Fri Apr 12 or Mon Apr 15.

Attachments: orchid_workload_samples.csv (sample traffic), call_recording_20290409.wav (meeting recording)

If the above looks right, I’ll schedule the deep-dive and allocate engineering time for the benchmark.

— Ben

Thanks Ben — putting a few technical clarifications inline. Quoting your note for context.

> - Sustained baseline QPS ~250 req/s with short promotional bursts up to ~400–450 req/s

From our ops playbook: baseline of 250 sustained in EU is comfortably handled with a small Dedicated pool if requests are batched modestly (batch windows 10–30ms). The bigger risk is the short bursts — we should plan a warm overflow pool sized for ~1.5x expected burst concurrency and an automated routing policy that moves overflow to the quantized 13B variant.

> - Mixed model footprint: primary model is a fine-tuned 33B variant for quality; exploring a 7–13B distilled path for cheaper low-fidelity responses.

Worth capturing: the 33B requires NVMe-backed KV cache to hit <100ms p95 at ~80 token requests. 13B quantized can hit 70–80ms p95 with much lower memory and cheaper GPU types. We will include both kernel/quantization profiles in the benchmark.

> - Autoscaling: reserved baseline + short-lived burst pool with warm replicas; target cold-starts <150ms for loading quantized variants.

We’ll validate cold-start numbers in the benchmark. If Orchid can tolerate a small fraction of requests at slightly higher latency during cold starts, we can keep burst pool smaller and rely on rapid warm-up (under 90s). Otherwise we recommend pre-warmed burst capacity.

I’ll draft a quick benchmark matrix (latency p50/p95, throughput, cost/unit) and attach to the deep-dive.

— Jasmine

Hi team — quick answers to your questions and a few clarifications from our infra lead.

- Current observed latency: p95 ~85ms (EU staging), p99 spikes to ~220ms under heavy promos.
- Burst characteristics: typical promo lasts 3–7 minutes, origin: campaign microservice fanout. 99th percentile promo bursts hit ~420 req/s.
- Models: yes — primary is a homegrown fine-tuned 33B. We have a distilled 11B candidate but it hasn't been validated in production.
- Data residency: production must stay in EU. Test/dev can use US.
- Security: we have a vendor questionnaire and a few artifacts — attaching the latest doc (orchid_security_q.docx). SOC 2 is expected Q3.

Also: our infra lead asked whether Redwood supports per-tenant KV cache isolation (we'd like isolation for privacy) and KMS with customer-managed keys. If you can confirm those in the deep-dive that would be ideal.

We are available for the deep-dive on Fri Apr 12 09:00–11:00 CET or Mon Apr 15 14:00–16:00 CET.

Thanks — Emily
